passage: The Okonkwo group investigated turnover of HIF-1α, a regulatory protein that is rapidly degraded in proliferating cells. To measure stability without confounding new synthesis, cells were treated with cycloheximide, an inhibitor of translation elongation, and harvested at the times shown. Lysates were resolved by SDS-PAGE, transferred to a membrane, and probed with an antibody against HIF-1α; band intensities were quantified and normalized to a loading control. Degradation of HIF-1α was assumed to follow first-order kinetics. The researchers hoped to compare half-lives under normal and stressed conditions and to learn whether proteasome inhibition would stabilize the protein. Results from unstressed cells are shown; each value is the mean of three biological replicates, with errors below 5% of the mean. Equal total protein was loaded in every lane, as confirmed by the loading control. All procedures followed the laboratory's standard operating protocols, and raw data were archived before analysis.

questions.stem: What fraction of HIF-1α remains 90 minutes after cycloheximide treatment?
questions.explanation: At 90 min, two half-lives have elapsed (100 → 50 → 25%).
questions.trap: Picking 12.5% (option B), the value at 135 min, or treating the decay as linear (75% or 50%); at 90 min two half-lives of 45 min have passed.

questions.stem: Why is cycloheximide used in this experiment?

options.A: It labels the protein for detection by antibody
options.B: It increases transcription of the gene
options.C: It blocks new synthesis so that the loss of existing protein can be followed
options.D: It accelerates proteasomal degradation of all proteins

questions.explanation: Without blocking translation, newly synthesized protein would obscure the decay of the pre-existing pool.
questions.trap: Thinking cycloheximide increases transcription or labels the protein; it blocks translation elongation so new HIF-1α is not made.

questions.stem: If the decay continues to be first-order, what percentage of HIF-1α remains after 225 minutes?
questions.trap: Stopping at four half-lives (6.25%) or overcounting to six half-lives (1.562%) instead of five half-lives at 225 min, which leaves 3.125%.

questions.stem: Which statement about first-order decay is INCORRECT?

options.A: The half-life is independent of starting concentration
options.B: The half-life increases as the starting amount of protein increases
options.C: The half-life equals ln 2 divided by the rate constant
options.D: The rate of decay is proportional to the amount remaining

questions.explanation: In first-order kinetics, t½ = ln 2/k and does not depend on starting concentration.
questions.trap: Missing the INCORRECT wording; in first-order decay the half-life is constant and independent of the starting amount.

questions.stem: HIF-1α turnover is typically controlled by which system?

options.A: Ubiquitination and degradation by the proteasome
options.C: Phosphorylation by glycolytic kinases that leads to secretion
options.D: Glycosylation in the Golgi apparatus that prevents degradation

questions.explanation: Polyubiquitin chains (K48-linked) mark proteins for proteasomal degradation; proteasome inhibitors such as MG132 stabilize short-lived regulatory proteins.
questions.trap: Choosing glycosylation, secretion or ribosome options; short-lived regulatory proteins such as HIF-1α are ubiquitinated and degraded by the proteasome.
